children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know a bit about your child (or children).

**First question: How old is your child?**

The age of your child is important because:
- Children **under 16** generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** typically don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have more than one child you'd like to check eligibility for, please let me know their ages as well.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old. I just want to make sure I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, who is 15 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, they fall into the automatic qualification age category. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

In other words, is Alex either:
- Not working at all, OR
- Working part-time (less than 24 hours per week)

Please let me know Alex's current work status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're still in school full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is not working, that's perfectly fine for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about benefits.

**Question: Is Alex NOT receiving any benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to confirm that Alex is not currently receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit
- Or other similar benefits in their own name

Since Alex is 15 and in full-time school, I would expect the answer to be that they're not receiving these benefits, but I need to confirm with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a regular 15-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships.

**Question: Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?**

Since Alex is 15 and in regular school, I'm assuming they're not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm. Different types of apprenticeships have different rules depending on the region (England, Scotland, or Wales).

Is Alex currently enrolled in an apprenticeship program of any kind?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. They're just doing their regular GCSEs at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, we can move forward. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively looking for work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do any of these situations apply to you?** Most people simply normally live in the UK - is that your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. We live in Manchester and have been here for years.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex.

**Question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You're considered responsible if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common situation)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

**Do you live with Alex?** Based on what you've told me so far, it sounds like you do, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me. We all live together in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! Since Alex lives with you, you're clearly responsible for them. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else who might be making a claim

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree with them to transfer the claim to you.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person who would be claiming?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. I'm the only one who would be claiming.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, we can move forward. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Question: Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- **Living normally at home with you** (most common)
- In hospital for an extended period
- In local authority care
- In a foster care arrangement

Based on what you've told me (that Alex lives at home with you in Manchester and is attending school), I assume Alex is living normally at home. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Alex is just living at home with me normally. Nothing unusual about the situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is living normally at home with you, let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final check before I can give you the result.

**Question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council currently paying for:
- Alex's accommodation costs, or
- Alex's maintenance/living costs

Since Alex lives at home with you and you're supporting them, I would expect the answer to be that the council is NOT paying for Alex. Can you confirm that's the case?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting them myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit! 

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex is a qualifying child** - At 15 years old, Alex is under 16 and automatically qualifies  
✅ **Alex is not working full-time** - They're in school full-time doing GCSEs  
✅ **Alex doesn't receive benefits** - Not receiving ESA, Universal Credit, or similar benefits  
✅ **Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - Just doing regular school education  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - Alex lives at home with you  
✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **Normal living arrangement** - Alex lives at home (not in hospital, care, or fostering)  
✅ **No council support** - The council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important Information:

- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: Be aware that if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay a tax charge
- **Payment frequency**: Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### How to Apply:

Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about the application process or Child Benefit?

All eligibility criteria have been met.

This is a straightforward eligible case.
